sanskrit: sīrāyudhas tadā rāmas tasmiṃs tīrthavare tadā tatra snātvā ca dattvā ca dvijebhyo vasu mādhavaḥ
english: Then Rāma, the plough-armed, the Mādhava, having bathed at that finest of fords and bestowed wealth upon the twice-born,

sanskrit: vanamālī tato hṛṣṭaḥ stūyamāno dvijātibhiḥ tasmād ādityatīrthaṃ ca jagāma kamalekṣaṇaḥ
english: the lotus-eyed one, garlanded with woodland flowers, gladdened then and praised by the twice-born, went on from there to the Āditya ford.

sanskrit: yatreṣṭvā bhagavāñ jyotir bhāskaro rājasattama jyotiṣām ādhipatyaṃ ca prabhāvaṃ cābhyapadyata
english: There, O best of kings, the radiant Lord Bhāskara, the maker of light, by sacrificing won lordship over the luminaries and his splendor.

sanskrit: tasyā nadyās tu tīre vai sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ viśvedevāḥ samaruto gandharvāpsarasaś ca ha
english: On the bank of that river, all the gods with Vāsava, the Viśvedevas together with the Maruts, the Gandharvas and Apsarases,

sanskrit: dvaipāyanaḥ śukaś caiva kṛṣṇaś ca madhusūdanaḥ yakṣāś ca rākṣasāś caiva piśācāś ca viśāṃ pate
english: Dvaipāyana and Śuka too, and Kṛṣṇa the slayer of Madhu, the Yakṣas and the Rākṣasas and the Piśācas, O lord of peoples,

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo yogasiddhāḥ sahasraśaḥ tasmiṃs tīrthe sarasvatyāḥ śive puṇye paraṃtapa
english: these and many others, perfected in yoga by the thousands, abode at that holy and auspicious ford of the Sarasvatī, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: tatra hatvā purā viṣṇur asurau madhukaiṭabhau āpluto bharataśreṣṭha tīrthapravara uttame
english: There, O best of the Bharatas, Viṣṇu of old, having slain the Asuras Madhu and Kaiṭabha, bathed at that highest and most excellent of fords.

sanskrit: dvaipāyanaś ca dharmātmā tatraivāplutya bhārata saṃprāptaṃ paramaṃ yogaṃ siddhiṃ ca paramāṃ gataḥ
english: And the righteous-souled Dvaipāyana, O Bhārata, having bathed there, attained the supreme yoga and reached the highest perfection.

sanskrit: asito devalaś caiva tasminn eva mahātapāḥ paramaṃ yogam āsthāya ṛṣir yogam avāptavān
english: And Asita Devala too, of great austerities, taking his stand there in supreme yoga, that sage attained the yoga.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasminn eva tu dharmātmā vasati sma tapodhanaḥ gārhasthyaṃ dharmam āsthāya asito devalaḥ purā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There indeed of old dwelt the righteous-souled Asita Devala, rich in austerities, holding to the householder's duty.

sanskrit: dharmanityaḥ śucir dānto nyastadaṇḍo mahātapāḥ karmaṇā manasā vācā samaḥ sarveṣu jantuṣu
english: Ever devoted to dharma, pure, self-controlled, one who had laid down the rod of punishment, of great austerities, even toward all creatures in deed, in mind, and in word;

sanskrit: akrodhano mahārāja tulyanindāpriyāpriyaḥ kāñcane loṣṭake caiva samadarśī mahātapāḥ
english: free of anger, O great king, regarding alike blame and what is dear and not dear, of great austerities, looking with even eye upon gold and upon a clod of earth;

sanskrit: devatāḥ pūjayan nityam atithīṃś ca dvijaiḥ saha brahmacaryarato nityaṃ sadā dharmaparāyaṇaḥ
english: ever worshipping the gods and his guests together with the twice-born, ever delighting in chastity, always devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: tato 'bhyetya mahārāja yogam āsthāya bhikṣukaḥ jaigīṣavyo munir dhīmāṃs tasmiṃs tīrthe samāhitaḥ
english: Then, O great king, having drawn near and taken his stand in yoga, the mendicant, the wise sage Jaigīṣavya, came composed to that ford.

sanskrit: devalasyāśrame rājan nyavasat sa mahādyutiḥ yoganityo mahārāja siddhiṃ prāpto mahātapāḥ
english: In the hermitage of Devala, O king, that one of great splendor dwelt, ever steadfast in yoga, O great king, who had attained perfection through his great austerities.

sanskrit: taṃ tatra vasamānaṃ tu jaigīṣavyaṃ mahāmunim devalo darśayann eva naivāyuñjata dharmataḥ
english: Yet Devala, though he beheld the great sage Jaigīṣavya dwelling there, did not address him in the manner that righteousness required.

sanskrit: evaṃ tayor mahārāja dīrghakālo vyatikramat jaigīṣavyaṃ muniṃ caiva na dadarśātha devalaḥ
english: Thus, O great king, a long time passed for the two of them, and Devala did not see the sage Jaigīṣavya.

sanskrit: āhārakāle matimān parivrāḍ janamejaya upātiṣṭhata dharmajño bhaikṣakāle sa devalam
english: At mealtime, O Janamejaya, the wise wandering ascetic, knower of dharma, would present himself before Devala at the hour of begging.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā bhikṣurūpeṇa prāptaṃ tatra mahāmunim gauravaṃ paramaṃ cakre prītiṃ ca vipulāṃ tathā
english: Seeing the great sage come there in the guise of a beggar, Devala showed him the highest reverence and great affection.

sanskrit: devalas tu yathāśakti pūjayām āsa bhārata ṛṣidṛṣṭena vidhinā samā bahvyaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: And Devala, O Bhārata, honored him to the best of his power according to the rite as seen by the seers, attentively, for many years.

sanskrit: kadā cit tasya nṛpate devalasya mahātmanaḥ cintā sumahatī jātā muniṃ dṛṣṭvā mahādyutim
english: Once, O king, a very great wonder arose in the great-souled Devala as he beheld that sage of great splendor.

sanskrit: samās tu samatikrāntā bahvyaḥ pūjayato mama na cāyam alaso bhikṣur abhyabhāṣata kiṃ cana
english: "Many years have passed while I have honored him, yet this listless mendicant has never spoken a word to me."

sanskrit: evaṃ vigaṇayann eva sa jagāma mahodadhim antarikṣacaraḥ śrīmān kalaśaṃ gṛhya devalaḥ
english: Pondering thus, the illustrious Devala, a traveler through the sky, took up his water-jar and set out for the great ocean.

sanskrit: gacchann eva sa dharmātmā samudraṃ saritāṃ patim jaigīṣavyaṃ tato 'paśyad gataṃ prāg eva bhārata
english: As that righteous-souled one was going toward the ocean, lord of rivers, he then saw Jaigīṣavya, who had already arrived there before him, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ savismayaś cintāṃ jagāmāthāsitaḥ prabhuḥ kathaṃ bhikṣur ayaṃ prāptaḥ samudre snāta eva ca
english: Then the powerful Asita, filled with amazement, fell to wondering: "How has this mendicant arrived at the ocean and already bathed?"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ cintayām āsa maharṣir asitas tadā snātvā samudre vidhivac chucir japyaṃ jajāpa ha
english: Thus did the great seer Asita ponder; and then, having bathed in the ocean according to rule and being pure, he murmured his prayer.

sanskrit: kṛtajapyāhnikaḥ śrīmān āśramaṃ ca jagāma ha kalaśaṃ jalapūrṇaṃ vai gṛhītvā janamejaya
english: His muttered prayer and daily rites performed, the illustrious one went back to his hermitage, taking up his jar filled with water, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa praviśann eva svam āśramapadaṃ muniḥ āsīnam āśrame tatra jaigīṣavyam apaśyata
english: Then, as he was entering his own hermitage-ground, the sage saw Jaigīṣavya seated there within the hermitage.

sanskrit: na vyāharati caivainaṃ jaigīṣavyaḥ kathaṃ cana kāṣṭhabhūto ''śramapade vasati sma mahātapāḥ
english: And Jaigīṣavya did not speak to him in any way at all; like a block of wood that one of great austerities dwelt upon the hermitage-ground.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā cāplutaṃ toye sāgare sāgaropamam praviṣṭam āśramaṃ cāpi pūrvam eva dadarśa saḥ
english: He had seen him bathed in the waters of the ocean—that one like the ocean itself—and now he saw him already entered into the hermitage before him.

sanskrit: asito devalo rājaṃś cintayām āsa buddhimān dṛṣṭaḥ prabhāvaṃ tapaso jaigīṣavyasya yogajam
english: Asita Devala, O king, the wise one, fell to pondering, having seen the power of Jaigīṣavya's austerity born of yoga.

sanskrit: cintayām āsa rājendra tadā sa munisattamaḥ mayā dṛṣṭaḥ samudre ca āśrame ca kathaṃ tv ayam
english: That best of sages pondered, O lord of kings: "How is it that I have seen this one both at the ocean and in the hermitage?"

sanskrit: evaṃ vigaṇayann eva sa munir mantrapāragaḥ utpapātāśramāt tasmād antarikṣaṃ viśāṃ pate jijñāsārthaṃ tadā bhikṣor jaigīṣavyasya devalaḥ
english: Pondering thus, that sage who had mastered the sacred formulas rose up from the hermitage into the sky, O lord of peoples—Devala then, to learn the truth about the mendicant Jaigīṣavya.

sanskrit: so 'ntarikṣacarān siddhān samapaśyat samāhitān jaigīṣavyaṃ ca taiḥ siddhaiḥ pūjyamānam apaśyata
english: He beheld the Siddhas who traverse the sky, composed in meditation, and he saw Jaigīṣavya being honored by those Siddhas.

sanskrit: tato 'sitaḥ susaṃrabdho vyavasāyī dṛḍhavrataḥ apaśyad vai divaṃ yāntaṃ jaigīṣavyaṃ sa devalaḥ
english: Then Asita Devala, deeply intent, resolute, firm in his vows, saw Jaigīṣavya passing on into heaven.

sanskrit: tasmāc ca pitṛlokaṃ taṃ vrajantaṃ so 'nvapaśyata pitṛlokāc ca taṃ yāntaṃ yāmyaṃ lokam apaśyata
english: And from there he saw him going to the world of the ancestors; and from the world of the ancestors he saw him passing on to the world of Yama.

sanskrit: tasmād api samutpatya somalokam abhiṣṭutam vrajantam anvapaśyat sa jaigīṣavyaṃ mahāmunim
english: And rising up even from there, he watched the great sage Jaigīṣavya going on to the much-praised world of Soma.

sanskrit: lokān samutpatantaṃ ca śubhān ekāntayājinām tato 'gnihotriṇāṃ lokāṃs tebhyaś cāpy utpapāta ha
english: He watched him rise to the blessed worlds of those who sacrifice in solitary devotion, and thence to the worlds of those who keep the fire-oblation, and from those too he rose.

sanskrit: darśaṃ ca paurṇamāsaṃ ca ye yajanti tapodhanāḥ tebhyaḥ sa dadṛśe dhīmāṃl lokebhyaḥ paśuyājinām vrajantaṃ lokam amalam apaśyad devapūjitam
english: The wise one beheld him pass beyond the worlds of those rich in austerity who offer the new-moon and full-moon sacrifices, and beyond the worlds of those who sacrifice with animals; and he saw him going to a spotless world honored by the gods.

sanskrit: cāturmāsyair bahuvidhair yajante ye tapodhanāḥ teṣāṃ sthānaṃ tathā yāntaṃ tathāgniṣṭomayājinām
english: He saw him passing likewise to the station of those rich in austerity who sacrifice with the manifold four-monthly rites, and so to that of those who offer the Agniṣṭoma.

sanskrit: agniṣṭutena ca tathā ye yajanti tapodhanāḥ tat sthānam anusaṃprāptam anvapaśyata devalaḥ
english: And Devala watched him reach the station of those rich in austerity who sacrifice with the Agniṣṭut as well.

sanskrit: vājapeyaṃ kratuvaraṃ tathā bahusuvarṇakam āharanti mahāprājñās teṣāṃ lokeṣv apaśyata
english: He saw him in the worlds of those very wise ones who perform the Vājapeya, the finest of rites, abounding in gold.

sanskrit: yajante puṇḍarīkeṇa rājasūyena caiva ye teṣāṃ lokeṣv apaśyac ca jaigīṣavyaṃ sa devalaḥ
english: And Devala saw Jaigīṣavya in the worlds of those who sacrifice with the Puṇḍarīka and with the Rājasūya.

sanskrit: aśvamedhaṃ kratuvaraṃ naramedhaṃ tathaiva ca āharanti naraśreṣṭhās teṣāṃ lokeṣv apaśyata
english: He saw him in the worlds of those best of men who perform the Aśvamedha, the finest of rites, and the Naramedha as well.

sanskrit: sarvamedhaṃ ca duṣprāpaṃ tathā sautrāmaṇiṃ ca ye teṣāṃ lokeṣv apaśyac ca jaigīṣavyaṃ sa devalaḥ
english: And Devala saw Jaigīṣavya in the worlds of those who perform the hard-to-attain Sarvamedha and the Sautrāmaṇī.

sanskrit: dvādaśāhaiś ca satrair ye yajante vividhair nṛpa teṣāṃ lokeṣv apaśyac ca jaigīṣavyaṃ sa devalaḥ
english: And in the worlds of those who sacrifice with the various twelve-day sacrificial sessions, O king, Devala saw Jaigīṣavya.

sanskrit: mitrāvaruṇayor lokān ādityānāṃ tathaiva ca salokatām anuprāptam apaśyata tato 'sitaḥ
english: Then Asita saw him having attained shared dwelling in the worlds of Mitra and Varuṇa, and so too of the Ādityas.

sanskrit: rudrāṇāṃ ca vasūnāṃ ca sthānaṃ yac ca bṛhaspateḥ tāni sarvāṇy atītaṃ ca samapaśyat tato 'sitaḥ
english: And then Asita saw him having passed beyond the station of the Rudras and of the Vasus, and that of Bṛhaspati—all of them.

sanskrit: āruhya ca gavāṃ lokaṃ prayāntaṃ brahmasatriṇām lokān apaśyad gacchantaṃ jaigīṣavyaṃ tato 'sitaḥ
english: And having ascended the world of cattle, Asita then saw Jaigīṣavya going on to the worlds of those who keep the Brahmā-session.

sanskrit: trīṃl lokān aparān vipram utpatantaṃ svatejasā pativratānāṃ lokāṃś ca vrajantaṃ so 'nvapaśyata
english: He watched that brāhmaṇa rise by his own splendor to three further worlds, and pass on to the worlds of women faithful to their husbands.

sanskrit: tato munivaraṃ bhūyo jaigīṣavyam athāsitaḥ nānvapaśyata yogastham antarhitam ariṃdama
english: Then Asita no longer saw that best of sages, Jaigīṣavya, fixed in yoga and vanished from sight, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: so 'cintayan mahābhāgo jaigīṣavyasya devalaḥ prabhāvaṃ suvratatvaṃ ca siddhiṃ yogasya cātulām
english: The greatly fortunate Devala reflected upon the power of Jaigīṣavya, his excellence in vows, and the matchless perfection of his yoga.

sanskrit: asito 'pṛcchata tadā siddhāṃl lokeṣu sattamān prayataḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā dhīras tān brahmasatriṇaḥ
english: Then Asita, steadfast and self-restrained, with palms joined, asked the most excellent Siddhas in those worlds, those keepers of the Brahmā-session:

sanskrit: jaigīṣavyaṃ na paśyāmi taṃ śaṃsata mahaujasam etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: "I do not see Jaigīṣavya; tell me of that mighty one. This I wish to hear, for my curiosity is very great."

sanskrit: siddhā ūcuḥ śṛṇu devala bhūtārthaṃ śaṃsatāṃ no dṛḍhavrata jaigīṣavyo gato lokaṃ śāśvataṃ brahmaṇo 'vyayam
english: The Siddhas said: "Hear, O Devala, firm in your vows, the truth of the matter as we tell it. Jaigīṣavya has gone to the eternal, imperishable world of Brahmā."

sanskrit: sa śrutvā vacanaṃ teṣāṃ siddhānāṃ brahmasatriṇām asito devalas tūrṇam utpapāta papāta ca
english: Hearing the words of those Siddhas, keepers of the Brahmā-session, Asita Devala swiftly soared upward—and then fell back down.

sanskrit: tataḥ siddhās ta ūcur hi devalaṃ punar eva ha na devala gatis tatra tava gantuṃ tapodhana brahmaṇaḥ sadanaṃ vipra jaigīṣavyo yadāptavān
english: Then those Siddhas spoke again to Devala: "You have no power to go there, O Devala, rich in austerity—to reach, O brāhmaṇa, the abode of Brahmā that Jaigīṣavya has attained."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad vacanaṃ śrutvā siddhānāṃ devalaḥ punaḥ ānupūrvyeṇa lokāṃs tān sarvān avatatāra ha
english: Hearing those words of the Siddhas, Devala descended again, in due order, through all those worlds.

sanskrit: svam āśramapadaṃ puṇyam ājagāma pataṃgavat praviśann eva cāpaśyaj jaigīṣavyaṃ sa devalaḥ
english: He came to his own holy hermitage-ground like a bird alighting, and as he entered Devala saw Jaigīṣavya there.

sanskrit: tato buddhyā vyagaṇayad devalo dharmayuktayā dṛṣṭvā prabhāvaṃ tapaso jaigīṣavyasya yogajam
english: Then Devala reckoned with a mind grounded in righteousness, having beheld the power of Jaigīṣavya's austerity, born of yoga.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn mahātmānaṃ jaigīṣavyaṃ sa devalaḥ vinayāvanato rājann upasarpya mahāmunim mokṣadharmaṃ samāsthātum iccheyaṃ bhagavann aham
english: Then Devala, O king, bowed in humility, drew near the great sage and said to the great-souled Jaigīṣavya: "I would wish, O blessed one, to take up the dharma of liberation."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā upadeśaṃ cakāra saḥ vidhiṃ ca yogasya paraṃ kāryākāryaṃ ca śāstrataḥ
english: Hearing those words of his, the other gave instruction—the supreme method of yoga, and what should and should not be done according to scripture.

sanskrit: saṃnyāsakṛtabuddhiṃ taṃ tato dṛṣṭvā mahātapāḥ sarvāś cāsya kriyāś cakre vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Then, seeing that one whose mind was set upon renunciation, the great ascetic performed all his rites for him with the rite as ordained.

sanskrit: saṃnyāsakṛtabuddhiṃ taṃ bhūtāni pitṛbhiḥ saha tato dṛṣṭvā praruruduḥ ko 'smān saṃvibhajiṣyati
english: Seeing him with his mind set upon renunciation, the beings together with the ancestors wept aloud: "Who now will share his portion with us?"

sanskrit: devalas tu vacaḥ śrutvā bhūtānāṃ karuṇaṃ tathā diśo daśa vyāharatāṃ mokṣaṃ tyaktuṃ mano dadhe
english: But Devala, hearing the piteous words of the beings as they cried out through the ten directions, set his mind upon abandoning liberation.

sanskrit: tatas tu phalamūlāni pavitrāṇi ca bhārata puṣpāṇy oṣadhayaś caiva rorūyante sahasraśaḥ
english: And then, O Bhārata, the fruits and roots, the sacred grasses, the flowers and the herbs cried out aloud by the thousands:

sanskrit: punar no devalaḥ kṣudro nūnaṃ chetsyati durmatiḥ abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo yo dattvā nāvabudhyate
english: "Surely the base, ill-minded Devala will cut us down again—he who, having granted safety to all beings, takes no heed of it!"

sanskrit: tato bhūyo vyagaṇayat svabuddhyā munisattamaḥ mokṣe gārhasthyadharme vā kiṃ nu śreyaskaraṃ bhavet
english: Then once more that best of sages reckoned with his own mind: "In liberation or in the householder's dharma—which would bring the greater good?"

sanskrit: iti niścitya manasā devalo rājasattama tyaktvā gārhasthyadharmaṃ sa mokṣadharmam arocayat
english: Having so resolved in mind, O best of kings, Devala abandoned the householder's dharma and chose the dharma of liberation.

sanskrit: evamādīni saṃcintya devalo niścayāt tataḥ prāptavān paramāṃ siddhiṃ paraṃ yogaṃ ca bhārata
english: Reflecting upon these things and the like, Devala by his resolve then attained the supreme perfection and the highest yoga, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ samāgamya bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ jaigīṣavyaṃ tapaś cāsya praśaṃsanti tapasvinaḥ
english: Then the gods, the ascetics led by Bṛhaspati, came together and praised Jaigīṣavya and his austerity.

sanskrit: athābravīd ṛṣivaro devān vai nāradas tadā jaigīṣavye tapo nāsti vismāpayati yo 'sitam
english: Then the best of seers, Nārada, said to the gods: "There is no austerity in Jaigīṣavya, who only astonishes Asita."

sanskrit: tam evaṃvādinaṃ dhīraṃ pratyūcus te divaukasaḥ maivam ity eva śaṃsanto jaigīṣavyaṃ mahāmunim
english: To that steadfast one who spoke thus the dwellers of heaven replied, "Not so!"—and they praised the great sage Jaigīṣavya.

sanskrit: tatrāpy upaspṛśya tato mahātmā; dattvā ca vittaṃ halabhṛd dvijebhyaḥ avāpya dharmaṃ param āryakarmā; jagāma somasya mahat sa tīrtham
english: There too the great-souled plough-bearer touched the water, and having bestowed wealth upon the twice-born and gained the highest merit, that doer of noble deeds went on to the great ford of Soma.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yatrejivān uḍupatī rājasūyena bhārata tasmin vṛtte mahān āsīt saṃgrāmas tārakāmayaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Where Soma, lord of the stars, sacrificed of old with the Rājasūya, O Bhārata—when that was done, there arose the great battle called Tārakāmaya.

sanskrit: tatrāpy upaspṛśya balo dattvā dānāni cātmavān sārasvatasya dharmātmā munes tīrthaṃ jagāma ha
english: There too Bala touched the water, and the self-possessed, righteous-souled one, having given gifts, went on to the ford of the sage Sārasvata.

sanskrit: yatra dvādaśavārṣikyām anāvṛṣṭyāṃ dvijottamān vedān adhyāpayām āsa purā sārasvato muniḥ
english: There, in a twelve-year drought of old, the sage Sārasvata taught the Vedas to the best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ dvādaśavārṣikyām anāvṛṣṭyāṃ tapodhanaḥ vedān adhyāpayām āsa purā sārasvato muniḥ
english: Janamejaya said: How was it that in a twelve-year drought of old the ascetic sage Sārasvata taught the Vedas?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca āsīt pūrvaṃ mahārāja munir dhīmān mahātapāḥ dadhīca iti vikhyāto brahmacārī jitendriyaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: There was of old, O great king, a wise sage of great austerities, renowned as Dadhīca, a celibate who had conquered his senses.

sanskrit: tasyātitapasaḥ śakro bibheti satataṃ vibho na sa lobhayituṃ śakyaḥ phalair bahuvidhair api
english: Of him and his surpassing austerity Śakra was ever afraid, O lord; nor could he be tempted by rewards of every kind.
